sources.entry: Zielzeit - Menu bar app projecting the year your Scalable Capital portfolio reaches a savings goal, read-only through the official broker CLI.

summary.one_liner: Zielzeit is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that projects the year a Scalable Capital portfolio will reach a savings goal, reading data read-only through the official Scalable CLI.
summary.what_it_does: Reads the user's Scalable Capital account through the official sc command-line tool, limited to five read-only commands (overview, savings-plans, transactions, holdings, whoami). From balance, savings plan, deposits and trailing return it projects an arrival year for a user-set goal and shows the progress percentage and market direction in the menu bar. The popover offers three scenarios (cautious 3%, moderate 6%, measured pace), two what-if sliders for extra monthly savings or a target year, and goal restated in today's money. It also shows each holding's contribution to the goal in weeks gained or lost. The interface is localized in English, German, French, Spanish and Italian. The README says the app has no networking code of its own and provides a make audit target that checks its safety claims against the source.
use_cases: Track when a Scalable Capital portfolio will reach a savings goal
See portfolio progress from the macOS menu bar
Project retirement or FIRE timelines from savings plans
Test how extra monthly savings changes the arrival year
Check which holdings moved a portfolio toward or away from a goal
how_to_run: make install (copies the app to /Applications; use sudo on a non-admin account)
make audit (optional: checks the safety claims against the source)
notable: Read-only by design: the README says the broker command set is limited to five enumerated commands with no write or login path
Includes make audit, a script that searches the source to verify the safety claims
Uses the simple Dietz method on measured deposits to estimate the realized return, with time-to-goal solved in closed form
Icons are drawn in code rather than shipped as image files
Stores only goal, language and an access flag in preferences, with no portfolio figures on disk
caveats: The app is ad-hoc signed but not notarized, so macOS shows a first-launch warning and requires a manual override in System Settings
Requires a Scalable Capital account, CLI access enabled on that account, and a one-time Terminal login with sc login --local-read-only
Requires macOS 15 or later; it is not sandboxed because it must launch the sc CLI
Projections assume constant returns and an uninterrupted savings plan, and are shown before tax
keywords: see when i reach my savings goal
